---
title: Publishing
description: How a remote or bundled plugin reaches users. Remote plugins are listed in the marketplace registry. Bundled plugins are merged into pku-harness-plugins and reach phones as a signed over-the-air update or with the next app release.
icon: Send
---

This page explains how a finished plugin reaches users. The steps differ for remote plugins and
bundled plugins. A plugin document is published by pushing its folder to GitHub; see
[Declarative plugins](/en/docs/build/declarative-plugins#publish) and the marketplace's
[submit flow](/en/docs/marketplace/publishing).

## Remote plugins

1. Deploy your MCP server over HTTPS ([Quickstart](/en/docs/build/remote-plugin#4-deploy)).
2. Make sure your MCP server's `name` matches the registry `id` you will use.
3. List the plugin in the marketplace. You can add a manifest to your repository and submit it on
   this website ([manifest reference](/en/docs/marketplace/manifest),
   [submitting](/en/docs/marketplace/publishing)). Or you can open a pull request that adds an
   entry to `registry/registry.json` in
   [`pku-harness-plugins`](https://github.com/pkuinfo/pku-harness-plugins). The
   [review policy](/en/docs/marketplace/review) explains how entries are reviewed and how the
   `verified` badge is given.
4. Users install the plugin from Settings → Plugins → Marketplace, or add your URL by hand.

Updates go out as soon as you deploy. The app picks up the new tool list the next time it refreshes
the plugin.

Keep tool names stable. Users' widgets and scheduled checks refer to tools by name, so renaming a
tool breaks them.

## Bundled plugins

1. Open an issue in `pku-harness-plugins` first. Say what the plugin does and why it has to be
   bundled.
2. Send a pull request with three parts: the folder `plugins/<id>/`, the entry in `builtinPlugins`
   in `plugins/index.ts`, and a registry entry with `"kind": "builtin"`.
3. Continuous integration (CI) and the reviewers run these checks:

   ```bash
   bun test
   bunx tsc --noEmit -p .
   bun scripts/validate-registry.ts
   ```

4. After the merge, the app moves its `plugins/` submodule to the new commit. How the change then
   reaches phones depends on what it touches. A change to JavaScript only is delivered as a signed
   over-the-air (OTA) update, which the app downloads and applies on its next launch. A change
   that needs native code waits for the next app release, which is a new APK.

Nothing is published to npm. The app and other developers use the SDK and plugins straight from the
GitHub repository.

## Renaming or merging

Users may have stored plugin ids, tool ids or widget keys in their widgets, checks or settings.
Never reuse such an id, and never rename one silently. Instead, use `PluginDef.legacy` to map the
old plugin ids, tool ids and widget keys to the new ones
([SDK → plugin](/en/docs/sdk/plugin#pluginlegacy)).

## Using PKU Harness Cloud

PKU Harness Cloud is our hosted service for features that need a server. If your plugin declares
`PluginDef.cloud`, copy its `cloud` declaration into the registry entry. The declaration has the
fields `uses`, `e2e` (whether stored data must be end-to-end encrypted), `disclosure` and, optionally,
`backend`.

The marketplace shows this declaration before install. `disclosure.zh` must say in plain words what
data leaves the device. See [Cloud → plugin guide](/en/docs/cloud/plugin-guide#6-registry-entry).
